The two calibration boards (rows) as the calibration of each of three lenses reconstructs them, from the photographs of one session. \emph{Surfaces:} every point of the planar board moved by the offset learned for it in the calibration with that lens, in the plane by the print error (aspect and skew) and along the normal by the height; the offsets are drawn 50 times enlarged, the colour is the height in bands of 0.5\,mm, and the dots are the $5\times5$ nodes of the height field. \emph{Maps:} the length of the difference between the offsets learned with the two lenses (in the plane and along the normal together) at every point of the page. Under each map: the RMS and the largest value of that length in mm. In each row the three surfaces come first and the three maps follow, one for each pair of lenses (Sigma 14\,mm minus Tamron 20\,mm, fisheye minus Tamron 20\,mm, Sigma 14\,mm minus fisheye).
